llm.summary: This appears to be an MCP workflow-orchestration skill, but it under-scopes external persistence and full-context logging in ways that could expose sensitive work data.

dimensions.detail: The coordination, subagent, pattern, and validation capabilities fit an MCP/code-execution workflow helper, but the role carries broad authority over tool orchestration and execution flow.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Automatic activation appears to rely on broad terms like code execution, MCP, tool chain, transform, optimize, break down, check, and monitor, which can route unrelated tasks into orchestration behavior without clear user intent.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No concrete install-time executable, package hook, or privileged installer evidence was provided; VirusTotal is pending and does not by itself change the verdict.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill examples reportedly persist intermediate results and emergency state externally, which may include prompts, file contents, derived secrets, or task state unless the user and storage controls are explicit.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The debug and recovery guidance reportedly includes full context snapshots and external state storage without clear redaction, retention, access-control, or opt-in requirements.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Use this only where you are comfortable with MCP workflow orchestration and possible external persistence of intermediate outputs. Avoid using it on sensitive code, credentials, private files, customer data, or privileged sessions unless you can confirm storage destinations, redaction, access controls, retention limits, and that subagent/tool execution remains user-directed.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] unexpected: The broad trigger terms are not inherently malicious, but they are overbroad for a high-impact MCP orchestration skill and reduce user control over when the skill activates.
[SQP-2] expected: Checkpointing and shared storage can be legitimate in large multi-agent workflows, but the supplied evidence indicates the examples lack sensitivity review, redaction, retention, and access-control safeguards.
[virusTotal.pending] expected: VirusTotal had no final negative result at review time and is not used as a basis for escalation.
